title: Cosmic Soil Upgrade — One Explicit Interacting Dark-Sector Benchmark
status: archive-generated cosmology benchmark extending the Infinite/Cosmic Soil branch; phenomenological interacting-dark-sector model, not recovered Great Book mathematics and not evidence for a common physical Soil
abstract: The Cosmic Soil branch becomes more useful by replacing a menu of possible dark-sector unifications with one explicit benchmark that can be solved and rejected. This record chooses a simple phenomenological energy-transfer law Q=xi H rho_c between cold dark matter and a constant-w dark-energy component using the parent record's sign convention. The background densities can be solved analytically, exposing the exact Lambda-CDM/uncoupled limit and the parameter combinations controlling departures. The calculation also demonstrates an important limitation: specifying the background scalar Q(t) does not define a relativistic perturbation theory. A covariant transfer four-vector, momentum-transfer prescription and stability analysis are required before growth/lensing predictions are meaningful. The model is therefore a benchmark for identifiability and closure, not a claim that dark matter and dark energy are literally one substance.

conventions.sign_meaning: With these conventions xi>0 transfers background energy from dark energy into cold dark matter.

analytic_background_solution.special_case: If 3w+xi=0, the integral becomes logarithmic and must be treated separately rather than dividing by zero.
analytic_background_solution.uncoupled_limit: xi -> 0 gives rho_c=rho_c0 a^-3 and rho_de=rho_de0 a^[-3(1+w)]. Setting w=-1 additionally recovers the constant-density dark-energy background.
analytic_background_solution.effective_dark_matter_equation_of_state: w_c,eff=-xi/3 at the background bookkeeping level
analytic_background_solution.warning: Effective equations of state are bookkeeping devices for background dilution and do not turn cold dark matter into a fundamental pressureful fluid.

background_observables.hubble_function: H^2(a)=H0^2 [Omega_r0 a^-4 + Omega_b0 a^-3 + rho_c(a)/rho_crit0 + rho_de(a)/rho_crit0 + ...] under a spatially flat benchmark unless curvature is explicitly retained
background_observables.direct_effect: xi changes the redshift evolution of the dark-matter density and, through energy conservation, the dark-energy density.
background_observables.degeneracies: Changes in xi can partially mimic changes in w, present-day density fractions and other cosmological parameters at the background level.
background_observables.rule: Distances/H(z) alone are insufficient to claim an interacting dark sector because growth and perturbation observables carry independent information.

positivity_and_domain_checks.requirement: rho_c(a)>0 and rho_de(a)>0 over the redshift range in which the model is claimed as a physical fluid description.
positivity_and_domain_checks.importance: A mathematically fitted parameter pair (w,xi) is not automatically physically admissible if the analytic solution drives a component negative or singular in the modeled epoch.
positivity_and_domain_checks.early_late_behavior: Inspect asymptotic powers a^(-3+xi) and a^[-3(1+w)] rather than assuming the interaction remains perturbatively small at all epochs.

perturbation_closure_problem.covariant_requirement: Specify four-vector transfer equations nabla_mu T_c^(mu nu)=Q_c^nu and nabla_mu T_de^(mu nu)=-Q_c^nu.
perturbation_closure_problem.decomposition: A general transfer can be decomposed into an energy-transfer part along a chosen four-velocity plus a momentum-transfer part orthogonal to it.
perturbation_closure_problem.missing_choice: The same background Q=xi H rho_c can correspond to different choices of transfer frame/direction and therefore different perturbation equations.
required_inputs: which four-velocity defines the energy-transfer frame
dark-energy rest-frame sound speed or underlying field model
stability over the claimed epoch and scales
perturbation_closure_problem.project_lesson: Background closure is not perturbation closure. Cosmic Soil cannot be promoted because H(a) can be written down; it must predict structure growth consistently.

nested_model_comparison.M1: wCDM with xi=0 and constant w
nested_model_comparison.rule: M2 must beat M1 on an observable not already absorbed by w freedom before the interaction is credited; M3 is required before using f sigma_8, lensing or matter-power predictions seriously.

distinctive_tests: Joint background-plus-growth inference rather than H(z) alone.
Posterior correlation of xi with w, Omega_c0 and growth amplitude.
Redshift dependence of the effective matter dilution exponent -3+xi.
Growth/lensing consistency once a covariant perturbation prescription is fixed.
Model comparison against xi=0 with complexity penalty or predictive validation.
failure_conditions: The preferred xi collapses toward zero once w and other cosmological parameters are allowed to vary.
The parameter region fitting background data produces negative density, unstable perturbations or other pathologies.
Different equally plausible Q^nu prescriptions produce materially different growth predictions that current data cannot distinguish, leaving the physical interaction non-identifiable.
The interacting model fails to improve prediction relative to Lambda-CDM/wCDM after complexity is penalized.
A successful phenomenological interaction is treated as proof of the historical Infinite Soil ontology.

external_references.use: Review of theoretical challenges, background dynamics, perturbations and observational signatures of dark matter-dark energy interactions.

external_references.topic: large-scale stability of interacting dark energy
external_references.use: Illustrates that simple interaction choices can generate perturbative instabilities and that carefully specified coupling structure matters.
